sections.heading: Repair Service

paragraphs: Per the file, epoch Slots: Each node advertises separately on gossip (per the file) the various parts of (per the file) an Epoch Slots: The (per the file) stash: An epoch-long compressed (per the file) set of all completed slots. Per the file, epoch Slots in gossip (per the file) are updated every time a node receives a complete slot within the epoch. Per the file, completed slots are detected (per the file) by blockstore and sent (per the file) over a channel to RepairService. Per the file, it is important to (per the file) note that we know (per the file) that by the time (per the file) a slot X is (per the file) complete, the epoch schedule (per the file) must exist for the (per the file) epoch that contains slot (per the file) X because WindowService will (per the file) reject shreds for unconfirmed epochs.

Per the file, every N/2 completed slots, (per the file) the oldest N/2 slots are (per the file) moved from the cache into the stash. Per the file, the base value M (per the file) for the RLE should also be updated. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Repair Request Protocols
paragraphs: Per the file, the repair protocol makes (per the file) best attempts to progress (per the file) the forking structure of Blockstore. Per the file, the different protocol strategies (per the file) to address the above challenges: Shred Repair \(Addresses Challenge (per the file) \#1\): This is the (per the file) most basic repair protocol, (per the file) with the purpose of (per the file) detecting and filling "holes" in the ledger. Per the file, blockstore tracks the latest root slot. Per the file, repairService will then periodically (per the file) iterate every fork in (per the file) blockstore starting from the (per the file) root slot, sending repair requests to nodes for any missing shreds.

Per the file, it will send at (per the file) most some N repair requests per iteration. Per the file, shred repair should prioritize (per the file) repairing forks based on (per the file) the leader's fork weight. Per the file, validators should only send repair requests to nodes who have marked that (per the file) slot as completed in their EpochSlots. Per the file, validators should prioritize repairing (per the file) shreds in each slot (per the file) that they are responsible (per the file) for retransmitting through turbine.

Per the file, validators can compute which (per the file) shreds they are responsible (per the file) for retransmitting because the (per the file) seed for turbine is (per the file) based on leader id, (per the file) slot, and shred index. Per the file, note: Validators will only (per the file) accept shreds within the (per the file) current verifiable epoch \(epoch the node has a leader schedule for\). Per the file, preemptive Slot Repair \(Addresses (per the file) Challenge \#2\): The goal (per the file) of this protocol is (per the file) to discover the chaining (per the file) relationship of "orphan" slots that fail to currently chain to any known fork.

sections.heading: Repair Response Protocol
paragraphs: Per the file, when a node receives a request for (per the file) a shred S, they (per the file) respond with the shred (per the file) if they have it. Per the file, when a node receives a shred through (per the file) a repair response, they (per the file) check EpochSlots to see (per the file) if <= 1/3 of the (per the file) network has marked this slot as completed. Per the file, if so, they resubmit (per the file) this shred through its (per the file) associated turbine path, but only if this node has not retransmitted this shred before.
